findings.title: Do not cache failed device admissions
findings.body: tagDeviceUI caches the device ID before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and returns nil on subsequent cache hits. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, this error return leaves that ID cached for 29 minutes. Retrying with the same ID therefore succeeds, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without admitting or counting the device. Populate the cache only after successful admission, and test repeated requests from a rejected device.

findings.title: Make the capacity check and admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without synchronization. With one remaining slot, concurrent requests for different device IDs can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Subsequent requests then accept both as existing devices, so the overage is not corrected. Admission needs database-level locking or another atomic capacity-reservation mechanism that also works across Grafana instances.

findings.title: Do not interpret an untagged request as an admitted device
findings.body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. A client can therefore omit this header and obtain an anonymous identity even when the configured limit is full, without being counted. Resource requests subject to the limit need an admitted device identity; skipping tracking must not implicitly authorize them.

findings.title: Enable environment overrides for the new setting
findings.body: The new device_limit key is read through iniFile.Section, but no entry is added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's regular environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI, so setting only GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT does not populate this option: it defaults to zero and leaves access unlimited. Add the key to defaults.ini or read the section through SectionWithEnvOverrides.
